issues.description: Method return type mismatch for PersonService.addParent(Person person, Person parent): The problem statement (Part 4) and the template declare addParent to return a Person (the persisted/changed person). The template signature is public Person addParent(Person person, Person parent). The solution implementation declares public void addParent(Person person, Person parent) (i.e., returns void). Call sites in PersonResource (e.g., person = personService.addParent(...)) and the tests expect a Person to be returned. This mismatch causes a compilation error at call sites and blocks students from running or testing the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution implementation with the template and problem statement: change the solution's PersonService.addParent signature to return Person (public Person addParent(Person person, Person parent)) and return the persisted person, e.g. add person.getParents().add(parent); return personRepository.save(person);. This preserves the existing callers in PersonResource and the tests and resolves the compilation error.

issues.description: The exercise requires a PersonService.addParent method that returns the saved Person, but the solution implements a method with a different return type. Concept: the service method that adds a parent to a person and returns the persisted/updated Person. Problem statement: describes addParent(Person person, Person parent) and states it should return the result of personRepository.save(...). Template repository: declares public Person addParent(Person person, Person parent) and returns null (stub). Solution repository: declares public void addParent(Person person, Person parent) (void) and does not return the saved Person. PersonResource in both template and solution expects a returned Person and assigns the result of personService.addParent(...) to a variable. This mismatch (expected Person vs implemented void) prevents a clear mapping between the documented API and the solution implementation and will confuse students and cause compilation/behavioral inconsistencies.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution implementation with the documented API and template: change the solution method signature to 'public Person addParent(Person person, Person parent)' and return the persisted Person (e.g., add the parent to person, then 'return personRepository.save(person);'). Update any other service methods and their usages analogously if similar mismatches exist.
